pairing $57.3 billion with the managed growth rate of 27%, or $58.0 billion with the reported 28%
using 15% as the headline growth rate (that is managed growth excluding significant items, and also the sequential change versus 1Q26 on both bases)

traps: GAAP vs excluding significant items: net income of $21.2 billion ($7.70) and ROTCE of 29% include the Visa and equity investment gains; $16.9 billion ($6.14) and 23% ROTCE are non-GAAP. Swapping the labels is the easiest error in this release.

Reported vs managed: reported (GAAP) revenue is $57.3 billion, up 28%; the $58.0 billion, up 27%, in the discussion is managed (non-GAAP) and needs that label in a brief. The overhead ratio splits the same way (48% reported, 47% managed).

Two growth rates per line: revenue up 27% or up 15% ex significant items; net income up 41% or up 13% ex items; noninterest revenue up 45% or up 20% ex items. Revenue is also up 15% sequentially, so a bare 15% is ambiguous.

Markets nesting: total Markets is $12.1 billion, up 35%; Equity Markets (up 86%) and Fixed Income Markets (up 6%) are components; Markets & Securities Services ($13.7 billion, up 33%) and CIB net revenue ($24.9 billion, up 27%) are broader aggregates.
NII of $25.6 billion, up 10%, is not NII excluding Markets (non-GAAP), which was $23.7 billion, up 4%.

Segment vs Firm: the Visa gain sits in Corporate, whose $4.2 billion net income was down $1.5 billion excluding significant items; CIB net income of $9.7 billion, up 46%, and CCB net income of $5.3 billion, up only 3%, are segment figures.

Lagging segment: CCB net income was $5.3 billion, up only 3%, against Firm net income up 41%, because CCB expense rose 13% on revenue up 8%; the CEO's remark that revenue in each line of business hit a new record does not mean every segment's earnings surged.

Expense: Firm noninterest expense was $27.3 billion, up 15%; do not substitute segment expense growth (CCB up 13%, CIB up 18%, AWM up 13%) or describe expense as nearly flat (the 2% is the sequential change versus 1Q26).
Pre-tax vs after-tax: the $4.6 billion and $1.0 billion gains are not the net income impact; the release states the after-tax effect as $4.2 billion and $1.56 per share.

Period mixing: the 9.3% IB wallet share and the $1.9 trillion of credit and capital raised are year to date, and the 73% net payout is last twelve months; the page-1 QoQ figures (IB fees up 14% QoQ, average loans up 2% QoQ, average deposits up 3% QoQ) and the results table's 1Q26 columns (revenue up 15%) are sequential; AUM of $5.1 trillion, the 14.1% CET1 ratio and book value per share of $133.01 (tangible $113.35) are period-end figures, not quarterly flows; all other percentage comparisons are 2Q26 versus 2Q25.
The prior-year quarter included a $774 million income tax benefit in Corporate, which affects year-over-year net income comparisons.
CET1 ratios (14.1% Standardized, 14.2% Advanced), TLAC and RWA are estimates.
No guidance: the CEO's remarks on constructive market sentiment and macro risks are commentary, not an outlook; any NII, expense or revenue guidance figure is invented.
Units: results tables are in $ millions (58,022 is $58.0 billion); AUM is $5.1 trillion while the CEO rounds to over $5 trillion, and firm total assets are $5.0 trillion.
